builds.howItPlays: You spend your early turns on spells that give you extra runes, such as Mobilize and Catalyst of Aeons, while cheap reactions like Flurry of Blades, which deals 1 to every unit at a battlefield, slow down your opponent's early units. Once you can pay 9 for Dazzling Aurora, it plays the first unit from the top of your deck for free at the end of each of your turns, and the one you hope to hit is Elder Dragon, a 12-cost unit that kills an enemy unit at every location when it arrives.
builds.whyYou: You'd rather spend the early game building toward one big card than fight over battlefields from the first turn. Playing almost no small units doesn't bother you, as long as the late game is yours: once Dazzling Aurora lands, you enjoy seeing what the top of your deck hands you for free each turn. Some games it comes down too late and you fall behind on points, and you can live with that because a board with Aurora and a dragon on it is very hard to beat. If a slow start that ends with a free big unit every turn sounds good to you, this Sivir fits.
builds.ratingNotes: Changed 2026-09-25 (re-rate from deck picks, style 'Dazzling Aurora Sivir'). The label stays Combo. Coordinates moved from 4.5/4.5/6.5/7.5 to 2/4/7/5.5 (pace/stance/complexity/variance), the mean of three scored decks from tools.ts style. Pace moved 2.5 and variance moved 2. The old numbers came from guide quotes that mixed a dragon/Aurora shell with a faster Miracle/Rhasa shell, while every current list plays no units costing 2 or less and steadies its draws with card flow. deckListUrl was the bare /decks page and now points at the display deck. Both old guides are gone: the riftbound.gg guide (updated 2026-05-18) lists OGN-183, Stacked Deck, which was banned on 2026-09-18, and the cardsrealm Miracle Sivir deck tech covers the Rhasa list, a different build. Scored decks: Best of Sivir CCS Houston (curator find; claimed CCS $25k Qualifier #5 Houston, placement unconfirmed; legal after the ban) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/72414274-4dd0-4172-b1e1-1cab164776f9 Combo 2/4/7/5.5; Sivir (curator find; edited 2026-09-24) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/618cc3ff-e6c6-4870-9da4-65a36efa7ead Combo 2/4/7/5; Aurora (themightythorge; filler with no evidence, it measures the style) https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/6103991d-40bc-4094-b8f1-5dd8d8f45fdb Combo 2/4/7/5.5. Adjustments on all three: complexity +0.5, because the Legend turns rune recycling into Gold and readies on enemy deaths, so Power payments and removal are timed around it; pace -0.5, because Forgotten Monument blocks scoring there until turn three. Deciding cards. Pace: no units costing 2 or less and 9 cards costing 5+ (Dazzling Aurora, Elder Dragon, Baron Nashor, The Harrowing, Mindsplitter). Stance: a single pressure unit (Sivir, Mercenary) against 5-8 removal and 9-11 reactive cards (Flurry of Blades, Gust, Lunar Boon). Complexity: 9 engine cards (Dazzling Aurora, Elder Dragon, The Harrowing loops) and 7-9 setup cards (Platewyrm Egg, Scryer's Bloom). Variance: Aurora's reveal-a-unit is the luck card, and 9-11 ramp pieces plus 3-8 card-flow cards (Lunar Boon, Scryer's Bloom) keep it moderate. Legend ability: when you recycle a rune, you may exhaust Sivir to play a Gold gear token exhausted; when one or more enemy units die, ready her. Also played: none. Confidence: low. For the reviewer: nearly all of the style's evidence is pre-ban and illegal through Stacked Deck or Aspirant's Climb, so post-ban results (for example the LA RQ) should confirm that Aurora Sivir is still played. The Houston placement is unverified.

builds.howItPlays: You put cheap units like Irresistible Faefolk on battlefields early, then use Ambush to play Nidalee, Cat Form or Rengar, Trophy Hunter as a reaction into a fight where you already have units, often on your opponent's turn. Punch First gives a unit +5 Might for the turn, so your opponent can never be sure how big a fight will get, and Sivir readies each time an enemy unit dies.
builds.whyYou: You like pressing from the first turns, but you'd rather win a fight with a surprise than by playing the bigger unit. You enjoy keeping energy up on your opponent's turn and dropping a champion into a battlefield just as they commit to it. You don't mind thinking hard on both players' turns, and you like that a well-read fight counts for more than a lucky draw. If ambushing your opponent sounds more fun than building one huge board, this Sivir suits you.

Adjustment on both: complexity +0.5, because the Legend readies on enemy deaths and turns rune recycling into Gold, which rewards timing kills and Power payments. Deciding cards. Pace: 7-9 units costing 2 or less (Treasure Hunter, Irresistible Faefolk, Tideturner, Dragonsoul Sage) and only 3-5 cards costing 5+ (Rengar, Trophy Hunter; Warwick, Hunter). Stance: 14-17 pressure cards and 7-10 tricks (Punch First, Ride the Wind, On the Hunt), with Ambush threats played into fights. Complexity: 18-19 reactive cards (Ambush from Nidalee, Cat Form and Kha'Zix, Mutating Horror; Hidden on Tideturner; Abandon; Flurry of Blades) and 16-19 setup cards (movement from Ride the Wind, First Mate, Flash). Variance: low, since the list is redundant bodies and tricks with no reveal or random cards. Legend ability: when you recycle a rune, you may exhaust Sivir to play a Gold gear token exhausted; when one or more enemy units die, ready her. Also played: Spiderling Swarm Sivir, the most copied Sivir list since the ban (about 10 exact reposts and roughly 20 close lists). It floods 18-19 Spiderlings face down to win fights or hold The Grand Plaza with 7 units, and it sits next to this Build (6/6/7.5/5): https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/bd922580-b62a-4f2c-b494-db305fbedf89 (sawadika, mylo_tcg, 36 likes), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/9967677a-3f80-41bc-9261-0b51e45553b2 (Spider-Sivir, dergermane050), https://piltoverarchive.com/decks/view/e32ee055-218a-4ec9-b3d8-50553459192d (Spider Sivir, alvl88pikachu).
